In this contribution, an overview of the regional preparations towards the WRC-19 conference are presented, highlighting discussions around the agenda item 10 being the placeholder for potential recommendations for WRC-23 new agenda item(s) on IMT spectrum in 7-24 GHz range. As the 7 – 24 GHz study item aims at new frequency range for the IMT allocation, it is worth to look at the related regulatory work and procedures towards the coming WRC-19 conference. According to the ITU Resolution 1380 [1], the agenda of the WRC-19 conference has considered identification of frequency bands for the future development of IMT, including possible additional allocations to the mobile service on a primary basis, in accordance with Resolution 238 (among others). Resolution 238 was to consider studies on frequency-related matters for IMT identification including possible additional allocations to the mobile services on a primary basis in portion(s) of the frequency range between 24.25 GHz and 86 GHz (i.e. above FR2) for the future development of IMT for 2020 and beyond. Therefore, looking at the WRC-19 agenda it is clear that there will be no binding decision taken during WRC-19 on the IMT within 7 – 24 GHz frequency range. Still, referring to the WRC-19 agenda item 10 (extracted below), the agenda of WRC-23 conference will be discussed during WRC-19. Agenda item 10 of the WRC-19 is the target agenda item for the potential IMT considerations in the 7 – 24 GHz range. Observation 1: Agenda item 10 of the WRC-19 is the target agenda item for the potential IMT considerations in the 7 – 24 GHz range. As per WRC-19 preparations, there are multiple regional discussions currently ongoing in following regional bodies, as listed in table 2-1. Table 2-1: Current status of regional WRC-19 preparations for AI 10 items on IMT in 7-24 GHz Observation 2: IMT-related agenda items for 7 – 24 GHz range for WRC-23 are considered only in selected regions. Discussions are still ongoing. For CEPT and ATU, summary of the input contributions and discussions around AI 10 and potential recommendations of new band allocations for IMT in 7 – 24 GHz range, were submitted in [2] and [3], respectively.

{"chunk_id":"R4-1909287-001","collection":"ran4_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Huawei"],"tdocNumber":"R4-1909287","title":"TP to TR 38.820: timeline of the regulatory work in ITU-R"},"point_id":"16696860630804165177"}
In this contribution, discussion on potential timeline alternatives for new agenda items inclusion for future ITU-R conferences, for IMT in 7 – 24 GHz range. Related TP to TR 38.820 is proposed for approval. Referring to the WRC-19 conference agenda in [1] (and extracted in Annex A), the Resolution 810 on “Preliminary agenda for the 2023 World Radiocommunication Conference” was allocated to the agenda item 10 of the WRC-19. Referring further to the content of the Resolution 810, it captures the following: “to recommend to the ITU Council items for inclusion in the agenda for the following WRC, in accordance with Article 7 of the Convention,”. Resolution 810 is provided for reference in Annex B. Therefore, AI10 of the WRC-19 is considered to be a placeholder for any potential discussions and decision on WRC-23 new agenda item(s) for IMT allocation evaluations in 7 – 24 GHz. Observation 1: Agenda item 10 of the WRC-19 is the target agenda item for the discussion and potential decision on WRC-23 new agenda item(s) for IMT considerations in 7 – 24 GHz range. As multiple WRC-19 preparatory discussions are still ongoing, it is still not clear which regions may submit to WRC-19 recommendations on the IMT-related new agenda item proposals for WRC-23 agenda. All regional inputs to the AI 10 (also including other agenda item inputs) will be submitted to WRC-19 for discussion and decision. Two timeline alternatives can be foreseen for the 7 - 24 GHz spectrum considerations for IMT: If additional IMT-related 7-24 GHz agenda item(s) will be decided during WRC-19 AI 10 discussions, the IMT in 7-24 GHz range will be further evaluated, discussed and decided during the next WRC-23 conference. If no additional 7-24 GHz agenda item(s) will be decided for WRC-23, the decision of potential IMT in 7-24 GHz range will be postponed to WRC-27, or beyond. Observation 2: in case of no consensus during WRC-19, discussion and decisions on potential IMT-related agenda items inclusion for 7 – 24 GHz range could be further postponed to WRC-27, or beyond. Based on rather long timelines of the above two alternatives, it is proposed to capture the above information on the timeline in the TR 38.820, for clarification and for future reference. Based on the above discussion and observations, the following is proposed: Proposal 1: Agree on the attached TP to TR 38.820, capturing two potential timeline alternatives of new agenda items inclusion for future ITU-R conferences, for IMT in 7 – 24 GHz range.

Wuhan, Hubei, China, 07th – 11th April, 2025 Agenda item: 7.15.3 Document for: Approval Test method for STxMP Sub-topic 2-1: MU assessment Issue 2-1-1: How to accommodate the difference from the core requirement derivation and test system restrictions including finite resolution. Agreement: The value for the uncertainty source of systematic error related to beam peak search is set as 0. The impact due to finite testing directions including limited choices for AoA1&AoA2 test directions can be handled in an additional Test Tolerance, TTFiniteRes. This additional TT should be determined in RAN4 and then communicated to RAN5 as recommended value to be added to the TT determined as a function of MU, i.e., TTTotal = x*MUTotal+ TTFiniteRes where x is determined in RAN5.

Changsha, China, April 15 – 19, 2024 Agenda item: 9.2.1 General aspects (work plan) [NR_BS_RF_req_evo-Core] Document for: Approval Introduction TSG RAN#103 meeting approved new Rel-19 work item “NR base station (BS) RF requirement evolution for FR1/FR2 and testing” [1]. This work item includes two objectives. Objective 1: This objective is related to expected EIRP mask for upper 6 GHz. WRC-23 has identified the frequency range 6425 – 7125 MHz which is 3GPP band n104 for IMT as in the ITU Radio Regulations (RR) footnotes 5.457D, 5.457E and 5.457F. The IMT identification comes with some technical conditions which includes the limits on the expected equivalent isotropically radiated power (e.i.r.p./EIRP) spectral density of IMT base stations for protecting Earth-to-space fixed satellite services (FSS) as contained in RR Resolution 220 (WRC-23) [2]. Objective 2: This objective is related to OTA test enhancement. Focus for this objective is on the OTA co-location reference antenna definition and improvements what could be done for FR1 for OTA testing enhancements. In this contribution we discuss work plan for these objectives which are the expected EIPR mask for the upper 6 GHz including challenges for this task and the OTA test enhancement. Discussion Expected EIRP mask The ITU-R Radio Regulation has introduced the expected e.i.r.p. technical condition for the protection of the FSS uplink (Earth-to-space) satellite receiver from the aggregate effect of IMT base stations. This is introduced through Resolution 220 (previously known as Resolution COM4/7) [2]. The expected e.i.r.p. values defined in [2] are as presented in Table 1. Table 1. Expected e.i.r.p. values for vertical angle range defined in ITU Resolution 220 [2] The goal for 3GPP via approved work item [1] is to introduce the concept of “limits on expected EIRP for angles above horizon” into the RAN4 BS core specifications and specify related BS test requirements in conformance test specifications. Precisely core part of expected EIRP mask objective of work item [1] is as follow: For performance part of this objective is as follow: It is important to do the measurements properly and diligently so that they are carried out in accordance with WRC-23 Resolution 220 [2] requirements and implementable with reasonable measurement complexity noting similarities to TRP measurement. The following elements are to be considered: Interpretation of WRC decision. Additional details and assumptions are required to address certain gaps in the technical condition set by WRC-23. Measurements over the whole band. Discussion is required about dividing the band into sub bands and conducting measurements over each sub band, e.g. 7 sub bands of 100 MHz each, or another sub band bandwidth or a more efficient approach. Adequate number of measurement samples to assure high confidence interval levels. The EIRP level stated is the mean value of EIRP (population mean). The minimum required number of measurement samples to assure a certain high confidence interval on the sample mean will need to be determined. Expected value of EIRP for an elevation angular bin needs to be calculated from discrete EIRP measurements. Therefore, the integral expression for calculating the expected EIRP for an elevation angular bin by averaging EIRP measurements over horizontal and vertical angles does not apply directly and needs to be replaced by an equivalent summation expression. Total number of measurements needs to be manageable while satisfying the requirement laid out by the technical condition of the expected e.i.r.p. defined at WRC-23. General propose work plan for expected EIRP mask is presented in table below: Proposal 1: RAN4 to agree presented work plan for expected EIRP mask. OTA enhancements Core part

SADC and EACO contribution in [1] was proposing new items for inclusion in the agenda for the WRC-23 to consider appropriate technical conditions and regulatory actions for identification of bands in the range 6 - 24 GHz for IMT allocation. This follows the previous African Region proposal at WRC-15. African countries submitted an African Common Proposal (ACP) to WRC-15 to include lower bands (~10 GHz) among those to be studied for IMT under the Resolution 238 (i.e. this resolution ended up with the range 24.25 to 86 GHz). This work item includes two objectives: one is related to expected EIRP mask for upper 6 GHz, and other is related to OTA test enhancement. WRC-23 has identified the frequency range 6425 – 7125 MHz which is 3GPP band n104 for IMT as in the RR Footnotes 5.457D, 5.457E and 5.457F. The IMT identification comes with some technical conditions which includes the limits on the expected equivalent isotropically radiated power (e.i.r.p.) spectral density of IMT base stations for protecting Earth-to-space fixed satellite services (FSS) as contained in Resolution 220 (WRC-23) [2]. Core part of expected EIRP mask objective of work item [1] is as follow: In this contribution we focus the discussion on the first objective which is the expected EIPR mask for the upper 6 GHz. Discussion Background of expected e.i.r.p. The ITU-R Radio Regulation has introduced the expected e.i.r.p. technical condition for the protection of the FSS uplink (Earth-to-space) satellite receiver from the aggregate effect of IMT base stations. This is introduced through Resolution 220 (previously known as Resolution COM4/7) [2] and the relevant excerpt is found in the Annex. The expected e.i.r.p. values defined in [2] are as presented in Table 1. Table 1. Expected e.i.r.p. values for vertical angle range defined in ITU Resolution 220 [2] The key requirements of ITU Resolution 220 [2] are: compliance with values of expected e.i.r.p above the horizon and providing a calculation methodology to the theoretical procedure given in the Annex to Resolution 220 [2] This expected e.i.r.p. condition proposed for the Radio Regulation is only for the top half of the hemisphere, i.e. above the horizon, and 360° (or 2π) around the azimuth. The angles for the ITU-R (Radio Regulation) are defined as described on Figure 1. Figure 1: Definitions of the angles defined by the ITU-R (Radio Regulation) Resolution 220 for the expected e.i.r.p. Observation 1: The key requirements of ITU Resolution Resolution 220 [2] are: compliance with values of expected e.i.r.p above the horizon and providing a calculation methodology to the theoretical procedure given in the Annex to Resolution 220 [2] In next sections we provide the formulation of the expected e.i.r.p. with some examples. The expected e.i.r.p. calculation The expected e.i.r.p. calculation is based on two averaging processes: Averaging of beamforming directions Averaging over horizontal and vertical angles Averaging over beamforming directions The initial ITU suggestion was a simple averaging process over a set of beams equally within the electrical steering range. This average power can be written as: However, the sharing studies in ITU-R assumes uniformly distributed UEs over the coverage cell which makes the beams steer with a non-uniform distribution over the coverage cell. To take account of this non-uniform distribution in the averaging, we can introduce some ‘weights’, wn, which can provide the adjustments. The beamforming directions have a uniform angular distribution within the steering range of the IMT base station. For a given vertical angle and horizontal angle with a sampling of beamforming directions , the equation can be written as: where wn refers to the weight for the th beamforming direction, i.e., the fraction of the steering range represented by the th beamforming direction.
